tier3_snapshot.observation_time_semantics: the Tier-3 panel content hash this row's features were read from; stamped per row so a --since-stitched table records which rows came from which panel build

tier4_forecasts.duplicate_policy: assumed unique by construction (one row per (ticker, event_date), the Tier-3 grain, totality by design per engine.data.features.tier4); not enforced by an explicit uniqueness check
tier4_forecasts.finality_semantics: A row's provenance is versioned by fold, not by a final/provisional flag: each producer's own *_fold_start records which strictly-prior-trained monthly fold produced it. Correcting Tier 2 at date D invalidates every fold from D onward; a rebuild's --since carry-over is refused (Tier4Error) if the carried prefix's fold boundaries, model id, or Tier-3 key coverage do not match the run about to happen.
tier4_forecasts.provenance_semantics: Per-producer *_model_id and *_fold_start name which registered model and which monthly fold produced that producer's forecast for this row; tier3_snapshot (per row, not per producer) names the Tier-3 panel content hash every producer in the same build pass read features from.
tier4_forecasts.coverage_semantics: Total over Tier 3: every Tier-3 (ticker, event_date) gets a row, forecast columns null where no forecast was possible (thin fold or pre-FIRST_FOLD). A missing row (not merely a null forecast) would mean the table is stale relative to Tier 3, which this schema treats as a build defect, not an expected state.

legacy_snapshot_metadata.description: engine.data.manifest.write_snapshot/read_snapshot's exact JSON, preserved byte-for-byte as a separate compatibility ObjectRef (phase-2 guide §5.1). 'snapshot' is a sha256 over the Tier-2 content hashes plus the Tier-3 panel digest; 'tables' carries per-table engine.data.store.table_stats(); tier4_sha256 is recorded beside, not inside, the snapshot hash so a champion promotion does not invalidate experiments that never read a forecast.
